findings.reason: the plan leaves one comparison operand's spelling unstated, and normalising the anchor through `_section_key` plus one case is the difference between the refusal firing and the duplicate being created.
findings.text: the refusal compares the requested anchor against ids `_section_key` makes of the plan side, but nothing in §4 normalises the requested anchor itself: an append anchored `s5.1` (the plan's own authored spelling, admitted by the shape guard's `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`) is not equal to the producible `s5-1`, so it is accepted and writes `id="s5.1"` that then sits beside the synthesis's own `id="s5-1"`, the collision the refusal exists to prevent; the ninth case tests only anchor `s5-1`.

findings.reason: a pre-marker append of that shape disappears without a record, which is the anchor-and-content loss §4 exists to end; naming the dropped producible ids is one field entry and one case.
findings.text: the "never silent" guarantee covers only unmarked ids that this run renders ("replaced by the rendered one", listed as a replaced unmarked id), but a pre-marker append anchored to a producible id the run does *not* render (for example a plan section id with no comments or runs, which the append could have taken because nothing rendered it then) is dropped by the legacy rule and named nowhere; the third case states exactly that drop as intended and asserts nothing about the result.
